research_notes: Obtain dated DFAT/PMO/NSW appointments, identify consulting/legal employers and hours, map BIT title and employing-entity changes, AITSL cessation and campaign leave, NSW Telco tenure and 2023–2025 work; confirm System 2 primary governance/executive records.

2026-09-29 initial avenues: frozen APH occupations; AITSL 2018–19 and 2020–21 reports; historical budget/control statement; first-person Asian Australian Project interview; Nesta speaker record; UK spin-out announcement; NSW Telco and network reports; full-time and employer searches. Large NSW annual report could only be read through indexed leadership extract; no unsupported full-document claim.

AITSL March 2019 start is supported; full-time campaign language does not prove previous employment hours. BIT had mixed ownership after its 2014 spin-out; ownership shares alone are not a control finding. Preserve unknown sector until relevant appointment and control dates are established.

CIN board interval 2022–July 2023 is not automatically NSW Telco employment duration. Guest teaching, school representation and governance excluded. No senior title or aggregate payroll/FTE statistic is used to infer individual full-time status. Partial record remains unresolved.

2026-10-01 follow-up: first-speech proof PDF and OpenAustralia, historical Board of Studies 2006–2008 and youth-council 2006 reports, appointment Gazette, System2 board and ACNC index. Added previously missing tutoring, projects, university jobs, Federal Law Review business management and advisory memberships; established precise Board commencement and primary charity directorship. Consulting searches still did not identify firm; Telco searches did not resolve tenure/2023–2025 gaps. ACNC full record inaccessible, and NSW PDF follow-up redirects failed; indexed primary extracts and available copies documented without bypass.

Next priorities: Federal Law Review mastheads or ANU archive and consultant employer name; Hurlstone tutor and education-project terms; shopping-centre/catering/tennis employers; dated PMO/DFAT/BIT/NSW appointments and individual hours/leave; AITSL cessation and Telco/post-July2023 work. Point-in-time reports and intended board expiry must not be used as employment endpoints.

Second follow-up2October2026: employer update reports materially anchor BIT principal adviser/ASK transition by2015 and Productivity directorship in2015–16. Their programme descriptions supply no ordinary hours, leave or personal contract boundaries. Searches under Xian-Zhi Soon and Zhi Soon did not identify private consulting employer or Telco/post2023 dates. Public old LinkedIn identifies ANU business manager but lacks dates and detailed provenance linking it to the Federal Law Review role, so no new ANU salaried employment invented; AI profile mirror discarded. Research paper affiliation is further BIT point evidence, not separate university employment. Next leads: BIT personnel/director appointment notices and historical corporate control terms; Federal Law Review mastheads, named consulting clients/contracts and Telco appointment/exit notices.

Third follow-up3October2026: AITSL's primary2020–21 annual report materially anchors continued General Manager, Evidence and Impact service as at30June2021. It narrows the previously open March2019-to-campaign interval but does not supply a cessation date or personal hours; aggregate organisation headcount/FTE was not attributed to him. Searches for a2021–22 personal listing, AITSL departure, NSW Telco appointment/exit, private consulting firm and BIT appointment instrument produced only already recorded reports and role summaries. Retain the exact AITSL point, leave end/hours unknown, and advance to the next member.
